partner_context.their_ambition: BC Ferries is the largest ferry operator in Canada, carrying ~20M+ passengers a year across coastal British Columbia, with a live program to electrify and modernize its aging fleet (the hybrid Island Class).
partner_context.their_pressure: Major terminals (Tsawwassen, Swartz Bay) sit far from the Vancouver and Victoria downtowns, the car-ferry crossings are slow, the Gulf Islands are served infrequently, and electrification of the big vessels is costly and slow.
partner_context.where_navier_fits: A foiling passenger fleet that adds fast downtown-to-downtown connections, serves the Gulf Islands cleanly and frequently, and advances the electrification program — with only a berth pedestal ashore.

hero.eyebrow: Authority proposal · British Columbia, Canada · BC Ferries
hero.title: Coastal British Columbia, on foils.
hero.subtitle: A fast, clean foiling passenger layer for Canada's largest ferry network.
hero.what_we_do_together: BC Ferries brings the coastal routes, terminals and ridership plus a live fleet-electrification program; Navier brings a foiling passenger fleet that adds fast city-centre connections and serves the Gulf Islands cleanly — without new roads or bridges.

why_now: BC Ferries has a legislated fleet-modernization and electrification mandate, Vancouver–Victoria road/ferry travel is slow and congested, and the Gulf Islands need better service — the moment for a fast clean foiling passenger layer is now.
multimodal_fit: Coastal BC commuters already chain SkyTrain, bus and ferry; a foiling pier slots into the same trip — transit to the harbour, foil across the strait, onward — adding fast downtown-to-downtown water capacity the car ferries can't.

differentiation.why_navier: A software-defined, autonomy-ready foiling passenger platform that adds fast clean capacity with only a berth pedestal — advancing the electrification mandate without re-powering car ferries, serving downtowns the big terminals can't reach, and with far lower wake on sensitive coastal habitat.

proof_points.claim: BC Ferries is Canada's largest ferry operator.
proof_points.evidence: ~20M+ annual passengers across coastal British Columbia on an aging fleet.

proof_points.claim: Fleet electrification is mandated and underway.
proof_points.evidence: The hybrid Island Class and a modernization program create direct alignment for zero-emission foiling vessels.

proof_points.claim: Terminals are far from the downtowns.
proof_points.evidence: Tsawwassen and Swartz Bay are suburban, making downtown-to-downtown a slow multi-leg journey a fast passenger ferry can leapfrog.
Infrequent car ferries leave the islands ripe for a frequent clean foiling passenger network.

objections.concern: BC Ferries runs car ferries; foiling is passenger-only.
objections.response: Correct — Navier supplements the car ferries with fast passenger service the big vessels can't economically run (downtown-to-downtown, frequent island hops).

objections.concern: The Strait of Georgia has open-water weather.
objections.response: Foils ride above the chop; Quanta-LR hybrid suits the crossing distances, and software-defined routing flexes with conditions across a largely sheltered coast.
We start with a fast passenger pilot (downtown Vancouver↔Victoria) to prove the model before any fleet decision.

objections.concern: Marine-mammal and wake rules are strict.
objections.response: Zero-wake foiling is far gentler on the Salish Sea's orca habitat than planing craft — an environmental advantage.

the_ask.partner_brings: BC Ferries brings the routes, terminals, ridership base, electrification mandate and public-transit integration.

close.title: Coastal BC, faster and cleaner.
close.body: A foiling passenger layer that adds fast downtown-to-downtown crossings and serves the Gulf Islands cleanly — advancing BC Ferries' electrification without new infrastructure.

why_navier_now.step_change: Hydrofoiling lifts the hull clear of the water, so a Navier vessel flies instead of plowing through chop - roughly 10x more efficient than a conventional planing boat, faster (30+ kt cruise), and dramatically smoother and quieter. It's software-defined and autonomy-ready, so the same fleet keeps getting better and cheaper to run over time. A step-change in marine mobility, not an incremental faster boat.
why_navier_now.no_new_infrastructure: Navier rides on infrastructure that already exists - the open ocean and the berths and jetties already in use. No vertiports, no new rights-of-way, no tunnels or tracks. Pioneer II needs only a berth pedestal; the Quanta-LR hybrid needs no charging infrastructure at all. That's the fundamental contrast with flying taxis and other new-infrastructure modes: nothing to permit, build, or wait for.
why_navier_now.the_moment: BC Ferries' fleet-electrification mandate, slow downtown-to-downtown travel, and under-served Gulf Islands converge — a foiling passenger fleet delivers fast clean capacity now.

end_state.headline: The fast, clean water layer of coastal BC transit.

end_state.narrative: A foiling passenger network runs across coastal BC integrated with BC Ferries — fast downtown-to-downtown crossings, a frequent zero-wake Gulf Islands service, and clean strait crossings — advancing the electrification mandate the big car ferries can't meet quickly.

levers: Navier is not proposing a novelty for British Columbia. BC Ferries already runs a zero-emission fleet program and the province already mandates deep marine-emission cuts. What is missing is a fast, low-wake, zero-emission passenger tier above the vehicle-ferry network — downtown Vancouver to downtown Victoria and Nanaimo, and quiet connectors across the Gulf Islands — that advances CleanBC targets while serving trips the car-ferry fleet cannot.

A zero-emission, foiling fast-passenger tier advances the 2030 CleanBC target and the 2050 net-zero goal directly, while adding faster downtown-to-downtown passenger crossings that the vehicle-ferry fleet cannot serve.
